core_obligations: Identify the class of the given extension in Ext^1(M, K) with the image of the identity map of K under the connecting homomorphism (proof lines 17819-17821).

Use the hypothesis that M is I-projective to conclude that this class is annihilated by every a in I, hence that a times the identity of K lies in the image of the map induced by K to P (proof lines 17821-17823).
Read off that multiplication by a on K factors through K to P and conclude that K is I-projective (proof lines 17823-17824).

difficulty_reason: The lemma is a closure property for the near-projective modules of the section: in a short exact sequence 0 to K to P to M to 0 with P projective and M annihilated by the ideal I up to the near-projective condition, the kernel K is itself I-projective. The statement is stated for an arbitrary short exact sequence with P projective (statement lines 17809-17816). The proof is a 6-line argument (proof lines 17819-17824) which reads the class of the given extension as the image of the identity of K under the connecting map into Ext^1(M, K), uses the hypothesis that this class is annihilated by every a in I, and concludes that multiplication by a on K factors through P, which is the definition of I-projectivity. What has to be seen is the identification of the extension class with the image of the identity, and the translation of the annihilation statement into the factorisation property; both are standard but neither is spelled out.
